neighbours.label: the comparison word right before the standard a thing is compared with: 'as' in 'white as snow' or 'as blue as the sea', 'than' after a comparative, and the same marker in French, German and Spanish (que, wie, como); 'as' for a role or a time, 'rather than' and sentences with no comparison stay low
fire: The bread came out hard as a rock.
This winter has been colder than any I remember.
Her eyes were as blue as the sea.
Il est plus rapide que son frère.
Sie ist so stark wie ein Bär.
Es tan alto como su padre.
The new phone is lighter than a paperback.
He ran faster than anyone on the team.
quiet: The bread came out of the oven as we arrived.
This winter, rather than ski, we stayed home.
She worked as a lifeguard by the sea.
Il est arrivé avec son frère.
Sie ist stark und mag Bären.
Es alto y vive con su padre.
The new phone came with a paperback manual.
He ran the drills with everyone on the team.

short: the comparison marker (as, than, que, wie)
notes: Found by an analogy concept screen (discovery only): 12/12 'as ADJ as a NOUN' simile pairs, peaking on the second 'as'. Card: max 100, density 0.11%; peaks ' as' x11, ' than' x9, ' comme' x2, ' que' x2, ' like' x2 ('white as snow', 'braver than this', 'Thick as a Brick'). Triage probes (exploratory, none reused): 'white as chalk' 1.00, 'hotter than a stove' 0.65, 'taller than' 0.43, German 'so groß wie' 0.60, French 'plus grande que' 0.38; role 'as' 0.03, temporal 'as soon as' 0.04, 'rather than' 0.02. Scoring runs on a Modal L40S (bfloat16; PARITY OK on Modal).
